text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- German chemical group Hoechst to announce today a buyout offer for Roussel Uclaf minority shareholders' stakes for about 17 to 20 billion francs. Hoechst already owns 56 percent of Roussel Uclaf (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, THe International Herald Tribune.)

-- Daewoo Electronics chairman Soonhoon Bae says maintains offer for Thomson Multimedia, does not rule out seeking French partners, also denies danger of technology transfers some feared linked to a Daewoo takeover. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, The International Herald Tribune.)
LES ECHOS
-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis to launch assessment of state's wealth in various fields such as buildings, artworks, infrastructure.
-- Bourgoin poultry group achieves a 160 million francs recapitalisation, but remains fragile.
LA TRIBUNE
-- National Assembly to look at bill against illegal labour today.
-- An executive reshuffling is expected at Credit Lyonnais in the U.S., Asia and France.
-- Employment association expects job offers for executives throughout Europe to increase by 13 percent in 1997.
-- Canal Plus signs agreement with 20th Century Fox on rights for encrypted broadcasts of Fox films.
L'AGEFI
-- International experts say future European single currency may finance up to 25 percent of world trade.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Pechiney announces it pulls out of bottle seal activity in France and intends to sell U.S. steel distributor subsidiary Intsel.
LIBERATION (Economic section)

-- Earnings of cattle raisers and meat producers expected to remain stable for 1996 despite the crisis linked to BSE "mad cow" disease, thanks to state subsidies. Milk producers to be hardest hit as they receive less state support.
-- Normandy town of Rouen blocked by public transport drivers on strike for early retirement and shorter work week.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Remy Cointreau first-half profit fell 81 percent to 41 million francs, sales rose 4 percent to 3.07 billion francs.
